subject: Latency acceptance criteria & traffic-shaping plan — follow-up
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency acceptance criteria & traffic-shaping plan — follow-up

Hi Ava,

Great conversation earlier — thanks for walking us through the Veridian production profile. I promised a concise recap and the concrete next steps we agreed on related to end-to-end latency, streaming behavior, and concurrency. I attached a first-pass latency matrix that maps your request patterns to p95/p99 envelopes and suggested traffic-shaping knobs.

Key notes from the call (short):
- Target endpoints: real-time chat (streaming responses) and batch rerank (non-streaming).
- Current provider reports p95 ~ 180ms and p99 ~ 420ms for chat at 16 concurrent sessions; you observed spikes during peak bursts.
- Veridian target for go-live is p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 250ms E2E for chat (including network + model).
- Throughput: median token output per session ~ 60 tokens, average session length 320ms generation window; burst concurrency up to 200 sessions sustained for 3–5m and occasional spikes to 500 for ~30s.
- Streaming expectations: client-side streaming with chunked tokens; you require early token delivery within 40–60ms after model emits first token.

Open questions / assumptions:
1) Is the p99 goal strict for all regions or only for primary US region? (we noted multi-region failover may have different SLAs)
2) Can you share a 1-hour sample of production trace ids or a synthetic traffic profile (we asked for veridian-poc-traffic-profile.json) — that'll let us run an apples-to-apples hosted PoC.

Suggested next steps (action owners in parens):
- Provide the traffic profile JSON and a small trace sample (Ava / Veridian infra)
- Redwood to run a hosted PoC against your profile and report p95/p99, cold-start behavior, and streaming latency breakdown (Priyom / Ben)
- If hosted meets targets, draft a Dedicated capacity sizing and fallback plan (Monica / Laura)

Deliverables timeline: Redwood PoC results and detailed latency spreadsheet by EOD Friday (2026-12-11).

Attachments: redwood-latency-matrix-v1.xlsx (mapping of request shapes to recommended batching/kv-cache settings)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30m demo of the latency matrix if that helps.

Best,
Priyom Das | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
p: +1 415 555 0198

Subject: Re: Latency acceptance criteria & traffic-shaping plan — follow-up

Thanks, Priyom — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications:

- The p95/p99 goals are for our primary US region only for the initial launch; EU will be a relaxed target (+~30% for network variance).
- We'll upload the sampled traces and the traffic profile to the Drive link by EOD tomorrow; the traffic profile includes the sustained 200-concurrency window and the short spikes to 500.
- On streaming: client expects token-by-token flushes. The 40–60ms number is for the first token only; subsequent token latency can be slightly higher but should average <35ms per token emission after the first.

One more ask: can Redwood surface the latency breakdown (network + proxy + model decode) in the PoC report? We need per-hop numbers to validate where to add edge proxies.

I'll loop in our infra owner (infra@veridian.ai) to upload the profile.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the PoC.

— Ava
Ava Thompson
Head of Product, Veridian.ai

Adding a couple technical clarifications from the infra side — per our call notes:

- For streaming p95/p99 reporting we'll break latency into: TCP RTT (edge), TLS termination + LB proxy, Redwood gateway (request scheduling + batching wait), model decode (token emission), and client socket flush. We'll provide a waterfall chart in the PoC.
- Suggested PoC config: hosted endpoint with 12xA100-equivalent pool, streaming enabled, prefix KV cache on session start, batching set to target 8ms max queue time for low-latency paths. This config is a starting point to match your 120/250ms envelope.
- For burst handling: enable fast-evict prefix cache and short-lived pre-warmed lanes for predictable concurrency; we'll test both approaches in PoC and report p95/p99 under both patterns.

I attached a quick SOW draft with the PoC acceptance criteria and the list of telemetry we will produce (p95/p99 by region, token-level latencies, queueing histograms).

Ben Carter
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
